{
  "persuasion": "PERSUADED",
  "support_scope": "FULL",
  "rationale": "The exact entry identifies 'the way' as covenant conduct (the walk/manner of life). Jer 6:16 and Matt 7:14 directly present 'the good way'/'the narrow way' as something one must walk in to obtain rest/life, matching the Hebrew derek sense of treading/conduct rather than a spatial route or person. The chapter evidence establishes the same pattern from the first occurrence of 'the way of the LORD' (doing justice and judgment) through the two-ways contrast and the Acts self-designation, without contradiction. The christological reading is secondary application (Christ embodies the conduct) and does not displace the core lexical-theological identification required by the cited texts. No material assertion printed in the entry itself fails.",
  "book_core_identification": "The way = covenant conduct (the walk/manner of life measured by God's standard).",
  "book_secondary_elaborations": [],
  "unsupported_glossary_assertions": [],
  "chapter_only_objections": [
    "Chapter equates the three titles of John 14:6 as Torah embodied in a person and re-reads 'new' in Heb 10:20 as 'freshly slain'; these expansions go beyond the two-word entry.",
    "Chapter's highway (mesillah) vs. way (derek) distinction and wedding-garment application are not asserted in the glossary entry."
  ],
  "strongest_counter_interpretation": "In mainstream usage 'the Way' is Jesus Christ himself as the exclusive personal means of access to the Father (John 14:6), with secondary extension to the early Christian movement that follows him (Acts).",
  "counter_core_identification": "The way = Jesus Christ as sole path/means to God (and by extension the community named for him).",
  "counter_relation_to_book_core": "CONTRADICTS",
  "material_core_denial": "The way is not covenant conduct but the person of Christ as exclusive access route.",
  "counter_case": [
    "John 14:6 is the most-quoted text and presents 'I am the way' as personal claim with exclusive access formula.",
    "Acts repeatedly uses 'the Way' as a proper name for the Jesus-movement, presupposing christological content.",
    "Heb 10:19-20 speaks of a 'new and living way' opened through Christ's flesh, read as the person/cross rather than Torah-conduct."
  ],
  "book_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Directly accounts for Jer 6:16's command to 'walk therein' the good way and Matt 7:14's narrow way that is found and walked, language of conduct not of a person or spatial portal.",
    "Matches the first biblical definition of 'the way of the LORD' as 'to do justice and judgment' and the consistent OT two-ways moral pattern.",
    "Explains why the earliest believers could be called 'the Way' while still claiming to walk the old paths written in law and prophets (Acts 24:14).",
    "Requires no special pleading for the ordinary Hebrew sense of derek as manner of going."
  ],
  "counter_explanatory_advantages": [
    "Aligns with the dominant preaching and confessional use of John 14:6 as exclusive soteriological claim.",
    "Unifies the Acts absolute use of 'the Way' under a single christological umbrella."
  ],

    "Acts 24:14 (the Way = believing all things written in law and prophets)"

support_scope.description: Support for the exact glossary BOOK ENTRY only, never for the supporting chapter as a whole.

book_secondary_elaborations.description: Secondary assertions actually printed in the glossary BOOK ENTRY; exclude chapter-only claims.

unsupported_glossary_assertions.description: Material assertions actually printed in the BOOK ENTRY that the evidence does not support. Must be empty for FULL and nonempty for CORE_ONLY.

chapter_only_objections.description: Objections to applications or arguments found only in the supporting chapter. Preserved for later chapter review and excluded from the glossary scope ruling.

instructions: Return only the requested structured result. Judge the exact glossary entry against the strongest specific alternative; treat the chapter as evidence, not as an additional judgment target.
